title: Characterization of Intra-Cartilage Transport Properties of Cationic Peptide Carriers
protocol: Cut and remove fat, muscles, ligaments, tendons, and all other connective tissue to expose the cartilage from the femoropatellar groove of bovine knee joints.
Use 3 mm and 6 mm dermal punches to make perpendicular punches into the cartilage to extract cylindrical plugs.
Place the extracted plugs in individual wells of a 48-well plate containing 500 μL of 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) supplemented with 1% v/v antibiotic-antimycotic.
Slice each plug along the surface of the slicing fixture using a razor blade to obtain a 1 mm thick cartilage explant inclusive of the superficial zone.
Store the sliced cartilage explants individually in polypropylene tubes containing 500 μL of 1x PBS supplemented with protease inhibitors (PBS-PI, 1 PI mini-tablet per 50 mL 1x PBS) at -20 °C.
Thaw the explant-containing vials for 30 min in a 37 °C water bath prior to conducting transport experiments.
Dab cartilage explants with a delicate task wipe to remove excess 1x PBS.
Record the wet weight of each explant using a balance quickly.
Place explants in a 1x PBS bath immediately after recording their weights to prevent dehydration.
Prepare 30 μM solutions of fluorescently labeled CPCs by mixing 30 μL of CPC stock with 2970 μL of 1x PBS-PI in RNase-free polypropylene tubes.
Pipette 300 μL of each 30 μM CPC solution into separate wells of a 96-well plate, avoiding the edge wells to prevent evaporation.
Transfer each explant using a spatula to the well containing the CPC solution.
Fill surrounding wells with 300 μL of 1x PBS.
Cover the well plate with a lid and seal the edges with flexible film to minimize evaporation.
Place the plate on a plate shaker inside a 37 °C incubator.
Incubate for 24 h under gentle rotation (50 rpm with a 15 mm orbit).
Prepare serial dilutions of CPC solutions from 30 μM to 0 μM in 1x PBS-PI.
Ensure at least 500 μL of each dilution is present.
Add 200 μL of each dilution to consecutive wells in a black 96-well plate.
Duplicate the samples in another row.
Obtain fluorescence readings of each sample using a plate reader.
Plot fluorescence reading vs. CPC concentration and derive an equation for the linear portion of the curve.
Incubate the CPC stock solution under the same conditions as the sample plate prior to generating the standard curve.
Collect the equilibrium bath from each well in separate polypropylene tubes after 24 h incubation.
Transfer 200 μL of each solution into separate wells of a black 96-well plate.
Obtain fluorescence readings of each sample under the same fluorescent settings as for the standard curve.
Dilute the sample in 1x PBS-PI if necessary to ensure readings fall within the linear portion of the standard curve.
Reconstitute fluorescently labeled CPCs in 30 μM solutions using RNase-free polypropylene tubes.
Cut cartilage explants into half-disks with a scalpel while keeping them hydrated with 1x PBS-PI.
Glue the circumferential side of the half-disk explant to the middle of one well in a custom-designed transport chamber using epoxy.
Remove excess glue from the well to prevent contact with the diffusion surface area of cartilage.
Note the superficial side of the explant.
Add 80 μL of 1x PBS-PI to both sides of the glued explant.
Pipette liquid up and down on one side of the explant to check for leakage to the other side.
Readjust the explant and apply epoxy as needed if leakage occurs.
Replace 80 μL of 1x PBS-PI with 80 μL of 30 μM CPC solution on the side facing the superficial surface of cartilage.
Maintain 80 μL of 1x PBS-PI on the side facing the deep zone of cartilage.
Place the transport chamber in a coverable container.
Cover the base of the container with a layer of 1x PBS to avoid evaporation of solutions.
Ensure no direct contact between upstream and downstream solutions.
Place the covered container on a plate shaker to limit particle sedimentation.
Incubate for either 4 or 24 hours at room temperature under gentle rotation (50 rpm with a 15 mm orbit).
Remove the explant from the chamber after incubation.
Cut approximately 100 μm slice from the center of the explant.
Place the slice between a glass slide and a coverslip.
Hydrate the slice with a layer of 1x PBS-PI.
Image through the full thickness of the slice at 10x magnification to obtain z-stack of fluorescent images using a confocal microscope.
Open the image stack by clicking on File | Open in ImageJ.
Click on ‘Image’ and then click Image | Stacks | Z Project from the dropdown menu.
Input slice numbers from 1 to the final slice.
Select ‘Average Intensity’ under Projection Type.
Click ‘OK’.
Bring the two halves of the custom-designed transport chamber together to assemble and close the chamber.
Use washers, nuts and bolts to tightly close the chamber with a wrench.
Coat the inner space of the transport chamber with 0.5% w/v non-fat bovine milk solution in 1x PBS for 15 min.
Rinse the chamber with 1x PBS.
Using a custom-designed slicing fixture and a razor blade, slice a 6 mm diameter cartilage explant to a thickness of 500-800 μm.
Keep the explant hydrated with 1x PBS.
Create gaskets from rubber sheets using hammer-driven and dermal punches.
Assemble each half transport chamber including one large rubber gasket, one PMMA insert, and one small rubber gasket.
Place the explant in the wells of the plastic insert with the superficial zone facing the upstream chamber.
Sandwich the two halves together to complete the assembly and screw tightly using a wrench.
Fill the upstream chamber with 2 mL of 1x PBS-PI.
Observe the downstream chamber for leakage from the upstream chamber.
If leakage is present, reassemble the chamber by adjusting gasket position and tightening screws.
If no leakage occurs, fill the downstream chamber with 2 mL of 1x PBS-PI.
Add a mini-stir bar to both up and downstream chambers.
Place the chamber on a stir plate.
Align the chamber so that laser from the spectrophotometer is focused towards the center of the downstream chamber.
Place the signal receiver portion of the spectrophotometer behind the downstream chamber.
Protect the transport chamber from light using a black box during experimentation to avoid interference in fluorescence signal.
Seal the openings on top of the chamber with flexible film to avoid evaporation.
Collect real-time downstream fluorescence emission readings and ensure a stable signal for at least 5 min.
Pipette a pre-calculated volume of stock solution of fluorescently tagged CPCs into the upstream chamber to ensure a final concentration of 3 μM inside the upstream chamber.
Take 20 μL from the upstream chamber.
Add to the downstream chamber for a "spike test".
Collect real-time downstream fluorescence readings.
